reference_sql:
SELECT isoyear(order_ts) AS iso_year, week(order_ts) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-15 00:00:00'
  AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY isoyear(order_ts), week(order_ts)
alternatives: SELECT EXTRACT(isoyear FROM order_ts) AS iso_year, EXTRACT(week FROM order_ts) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-15 00:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1, 2

SELECT isoyear(date_trunc('week', order_ts)) AS iso_year, week(date_trunc('week', order_ts)) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-15 00:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY date_trunc('week', order_ts)

other_way.sql: SELECT isoyear(date_trunc('week', order_ts)) AS iso_year, week(date_trunc('week', order_ts)) AS iso_week, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-15 00:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY date_trunc('week', order_ts)
other_way.tradeoff: Grouping by the Monday from date_trunc('week', ...) gives the same ISO weeks, and you read the labels off that Monday.

solver.query:

FROM orders
WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-12-15 00:00:00'
  AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY isoyear(order_ts), weekofyear(order_ts)
